# ADR-0017: A claim is an event or a state; nothing retracts itself

> **Written `proposed`.** It depends on proposed record 0016 being accepted — it exists because that record deletes something — and it carries `<<SPIKE: …>>` places that a one-session spike is measuring now. Nothing is built against it until Kent accepts it with those places filled.

## Context and Problem Statement

Record 0005 gives every arrow a `mode`. A **`trigger`** arrow is a domino: it fires when its cause becomes true, and standing the cause back up later does not undo it. A **`sustain`** arrow is a desk holding an apple: the effect holds only while the cause holds, and take the cause away and the effect falls. Record 0005 calls that pair *"the best idea in the brainstorm"*, and Kent asked for it to be kept.

Proposed record 0016 deletes it — not deliberately, as a side effect. Under that record a claim's number is *the chance it has happened by day t*, and something that has happened never un-happens. The moment that is true, the quantity a `sustain` arrow reads (its cause's truth, read on each day) and the quantity a `trigger` arrow reads (whether its cause has fired) are **the same thing**.

**Measured.** In today's code a `sustain` arrow pushes with the cause's truth read on every day and a `trigger` arrow with a single fired-or-not flag per world (`backend/src/katalyst/domain/propagation.py:1431-1434`). They differ for exactly one reason: today a claim can **un-resolve** when an impulse fades (`:1444`) — which is the defect proposed record 0016 removes on purpose. Build both under first passage and they are not close, they are the same number: `0.442471` and `0.442471` on the map the check builds, because the two arrays are the same array. `mode` becomes dead data, fully determined by `shape`. (Re-run on 2026-09-21 by this record's author; the check is `attack3.py` section B, kept locally under `plans/analysis/scripts/redteam/`.)

The only mechanism in the product that can make a true claim untrue is **automatic retraction** — the rule of record 0014, which ends a supposition on a calendar worked out from the shape of the map. That rule is itself one of the three defects proposed record 0016 exists to fix. It cannot be the thing that saves `sustain`.

So: **does a `sustain` arrow survive, and if so, what does it leave?** The question is not optional and "leave it as it is" is not on the list.

### The second reason, which is the brief's own sentence

The brief's example is *"the Strait of Hormuz opened but Iran was struck the next day."* That asks for a world in which **both things happened**. Today the strike retracts the opening: Monday's event un-happens because of Tuesday's news, and the flagship branch's headline is a claim the reader asserted being deleted by a claim the reader inserted.

And the deletion fires on a schedule, not on anything real. Suppose the strait is open on 1 October, then add a claim the map gives one chance in a thousand, carrying an arrow of `−0.01` into it: the tile never reads *Supposed* on any day — its day-states run `withdrawn, withdrawn, pushed, pushed, …` from day zero and its number is its own prior throughout (re-run 2026-09-21; `recheck.py` section 1, kept locally under `plans/analysis/scripts/engine/`).

## Decision Drivers

* **Record 0005's best idea, and Kent's instruction to keep it.** Whatever ships must either keep the distinction or say plainly that it is gone.
* **The brief's own sentence must come out right.** Both events stand.
* **The traceability veto** (Kent): no state that cannot be traced to an input, a rule or a cited source. A supposition deleted by a cause nobody believes is that state.
* **INV-3, assert is not observe** — *supposing a claim changes nothing upstream of it.* Deleting the supposition is a stronger move than anything INV-3 contemplates.
* **Pay once** (Kent, 2026-09-21): everything that changes what we ask the model lands in one freeze, and the four examples are recorded once after it.
* **The canvas is meant to be settling down.** A change here is worth having only if it is mostly *deletion*.

## Considered Options

The three Kent was offered on 2026-09-21, in the words they were put in:

* **(i) Events and states.** A claim is an **event** (once it has happened, it has happened) or a **state** (it holds over a stretch of time and can stop holding). A `sustain` arrow may only leave a state. Automatic retraction is deleted.
* **(ii) Events only; a sustained push is two arrows** — one from the event that starts it, and an inhibiting arrow from the event that ends it. Same arithmetic, one validity rule, one sentence in the prompt, no new field. `mode` and the word *sustain* leave the vocabulary.
* **(iii) Keep today's snapshot meaning, for states only.** Two meanings of a number on one map.

**Kent chose (i) on 2026-09-21.**

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"(i) Events and states"**, because it is the only one of the three under which the brief's own example sentence comes out right — both events stand, and what falls is the thing everything downstream actually depended on — and because it is the only one that gives record 0005's best idea something real to be about.

### What a claim carries

One new field on a claim, `persistence`, with two values:

| | What it means | Hormuz |
|---|---|---|
| **event** | Once it has happened, it has happened. Its number is the chance it happens by its deadline, and its curve only rises. | *The Strait of Hormuz reopens to unrestricted commercial transit.* *A confirmed military strike on Iranian territory.* |
| **state** | It holds over a stretch of time, and it can stop holding. | *The strait stays open to commercial transit through 1 November.* |

A `sustain` arrow may leave **only** a state. That is the whole of the rule, and it is what gives the word *sustain* a job again: a state can stop, so an effect that holds only while its cause holds has something to stop with.

**What a state's number means in the arithmetic is not settled here.** A parallel measurement is running now. A state that holds over an interval is not one yes/no fact: four maps in which *"did it ever hold?"* is YES in every row, differing only in when the state switched on and off, give the claim it sustains `.8269`, `.1483`, `.1934` and `.2151` — about `.68` of probability spread across maps that a single yes/no cannot tell apart (re-run 2026-09-21; `attack3.py` section C). So a state needs an on-time and an off-time, and the questions below are measured, not guessed:

* `<<SPIKE: what a state claim's number answers, in the one sentence the tile will print — "it holds on its deadline", "it ever held", or something else>>`
* `<<SPIKE: how a state's on-time and off-time are represented, and how many variables in the solve a state claim costs>>`
* `<<SPIKE: the cost of a state claim — milliseconds for one range on a 20-claim map carrying state claims, against the same map with none>>`

### The Hormuz strike, before and after, in the words on screen

**Today**, pinned by the golden test (`backend/tests/unit/fixtures/test_hormuz_golden.py:110-123`): the supposed strait claim reads **Supposed** on day zero, then **withdrawn** on days one to three and **pushed** from day four, and the tile carries the badge

> **Retracted · Oct 2 · by "a confirmed military strike on Iranian territory"**

The world carries one retraction naming the strike as the thing that revoked the reader's own supposition. The reader supposed a thing; the product deleted it.

**After this record**, the same branch reads as three lines that are all true at once:

> *the strait opened* — **Supposed · Oct 1**
> *a confirmed military strike on Iranian territory* — **Added**
> *the strait stays open to commercial transit through 1 November* — a number, which the strike lowers
> *Brent settles below $68* — a number, which follows the state down

*(Shape only. The numbers come from the engine when the flip lands, and the generated numbers file owns them.)* Both events stand. Nothing on the map contradicts the reader. What moves is the state everything downstream was resting on, which is the claim the reader should have been watching all along.

### What is deleted

All of this goes, and it is the reason the change is worth its cost — it is removal, not another guard on a canvas that is meant to be settling down.

* **The `Retracted · date · by "…"` badge.** `spec/vocabulary.md` calls it the one *derived* badge, the only one no button produces. It goes, and so does its entry there; its height is baked into the tile's geometry, which comes back.
* **Two of the four day-states.** `SeriesState` is `sampled · supposed · withdrawn · pushed` (`propagation.py:90`); `withdrawn` and `pushed` go and the first two remain. This is cheap: the browser has exactly one live reader of the day-states and it tests for `"supposed"` alone (`frontend/src/world/apiSource.ts:194`, checked on `main`).
* **Retraction by calendar, entirely** — the test for which arrows oppose a supposition, the undermining half of the rule that lays out a supposition's spells, the code that builds the retractions, and the `Retraction` model on the wire (`propagation.py:147`, `:888-895`, `:940-948`, `:962`).
* **With it, the third defect.** There is no schedule left to fire, so no claim the map gives a thousand-to-one chance can delete anything.
* **UX-14** as written — *"a claim the user supposed true, and that a later edit in the same branch has pushed back down, never renders as plainly true… its tile carries both states in order"* — describes a thing that no longer happens. It is replaced by a requirement about states: a claim that stops holding says when it stopped and what stopped it. The replacement wording is listed for the pull request that carries this record.

**This reverses decision A of record 0014** — *"a supposition is a hard fact in every simulated world, and it ends on the day the cause of the first live arrow pushing against it becomes true"* — and its three-state table, and its two confirmation tests `test_retraction_dates_from_the_cause_not_the_push` and the Hormuz golden series. **What stands from record 0014:** a supposition is a hard fact in every world *while it holds*; the tile shows the word **Supposed · date** and never a number. What changes is that nothing ends it but another edit.

**It amends ADR-0005's `mode` table** — the row reading *"`sustain` — the effect holds only while the parent holds; remove the parent and it retracts"* now reads *"…only while the parent holds; a `sustain` arrow may leave only a state, because only a state can stop"*. Its consequence bullet about the Hormuz-then-strike branch is restated: the pair works, and the thing it works on is a state.

### The new rules the map must obey

1. **A `sustain` arrow may only leave a claim whose `persistence` is `state`.** A twenty-first violation code, `sustain_without_a_state`, in the pattern of the twenty that exist (`documented_without_source`, `market_without_payoff`, `reflexive_without_lag`). Rejected, never repaired — turning the arrow into a `trigger` silently would be our code deciding what the model meant.
2. **Every claim says which kind it is.** No code in the pure core can read a claim's sentence and decide whether it names an event or a state; that judgement is the model's, which is why this field moves what we ask for.

### This field rides the one shape freeze, and record 0017 must be accepted before that freeze is written

Adding `persistence` to what the model answers moves the **prompt fingerprint** — the hash that says a recording was made by the program that is running now. Measured by the adversarial pass on 2026-09-21: `main` hashes to `1c224cc3…`, and with `persistence` added to the claim proposal it hashes to `1e80b47b…`. A moved fingerprint makes every committed recording stale.

Worse, and measured by this record's author on 2026-09-21 against the recording committed on the stack-04 recordings branch: that recording carries **19 accepted arrows, 6 of them `sustain`, and all six leave claims whose `kind` is `event`**. With the validity rule above in force, **all six become illegal.** So:

* `persistence` and its rule land **only** in stack 05's shape freeze, with the re-recording in the same pull request — never in a pull request that merges before the new recordings do, or `main` is green over a map its own validator would refuse.
* **This record therefore has to be accepted before the freeze is written**, not merged alongside it.

Everything else in this record — the retraction deletion, the two day-states, the badge — has no model in it and can land with the engine flip.

### Consequences

* Good, because the brief's own sentence finally comes out right, and the product stops deleting things the reader typed.
* Good, because it is mostly deletion: about 250 lines out of the backend and 120 out of the browser against about 60 added for the field and its rule (engine digest section 5.3, 2026-09-21). Set against those figures, a state's on-and-off representation has not been priced — see the spike tokens above.
* Good, because record 0005's best idea keeps its meaning instead of quietly becoming a synonym.
* Good, because the third defect dies with the schedule that caused it.
* Bad, because the model has to make a judgement it has never been asked for, and nothing in our code can check it. A claim marked `event` that is really a state will simply never stop holding, and the only signal is a reader reading the sentence.
* Bad, because it adds a claim to the Hormuz map — *the strait stays open through 1 November* — and every number downstream of the strait moves again for that reason as well as for the engine's.
* Bad, because a state costs more in the solve than an event, by an amount nobody has measured yet.
* Neutral, because the canvas loses a badge and two colours and gains nothing to draw.

### Confirmation

* `test_a_sustain_arrow_must_leave_a_state` — the validator refuses a `sustain` arrow out of an event, with its own sentence, and repairs nothing.
* `test_both_events_stand_through_the_strike` — on the Hormuz strike branch, the supposed opening reads **Supposed** on every day of the window and the strike reads as having happened; neither is withdrawn, and the world carries no retraction because the model no longer exists.
* `test_the_state_is_what_falls` — on the same branch, the state claim's number is lower than in the base world, and so is every claim it sustains. Directions and orderings, never typed-in values.
* `test_a_supposition_is_not_ended_by_a_cause_nobody_believes` — the reproduction above, turned into a test: inserting a claim at `.001` with a `−0.01` arrow into a supposed claim leaves it **Supposed** on every day.
* `grep -rn "Retraction\|withdrawn\|pushed" backend/src frontend/src` finds nothing outside history.
* The two oracles of proposed record 0016 run over maps that carry state claims as well as events, so the tolerance they measure covers both.

## Open for Kent

**1. The field's name.** `persistence: event | state` collides in a reader's mind with something that already exists: a claim's `kind` is one of `hypothesis · event · market · not_tradeable`. Under this record a `market` claim would carry `persistence: event`, and a claim of `kind: event` could carry `persistence: state` — the word *event* would mean two different things one field apart, on the same tile, in the same Inspector. This record is written with `persistence` throughout; every use of it reads as `<<SPIKE: the field's name, once Kent has chosen>>`.

* *Recommended:* keep `persistence` and rename its **values** so the collision disappears — `persistence: once | while`, read as *"once it happens it stays"* and *"only while it holds"*. Cost: nothing in code; two words in the prompt and three sentences in the chapters. It also reads correctly beside `mode: trigger | sustain`, which is the distinction it is really about.
* Alternative: keep `persistence: event | state` as proposed. Cost: nothing to build, and a word that means two things on one tile.
* Alternative: rename the field instead — `holds: once | while`, or `kind_of_truth`. Cost: the same, and `persistence` is the word both reviews and the design page already use, so every note would have to be reread.

**2. Whether a hand-written map may leave the field out.** The model always states it; a fixture is written by a person.

* *Recommended:* no default — every claim, hand-written or generated, says which it is. Cost: one line in each of the seven Hormuz claims and in the property-test builders. It matches *reject, never repair*: a map that does not say cannot be guessed at.
* Alternative: default to `event`. Cost: nothing today, and the first hand-written state claim someone forgets to mark is a claim that silently never stops holding.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### (i) Events and states (chosen)

* Good, because *"Hormuz opens, then Iran is struck"* leaves both events standing and lowers the state everything downstream depends on — which is what the brief asks for and what a trader would actually watch.
* Good, because `sustain` gets its meaning back rather than becoming a synonym for `step`.
* Good, because automatic retraction — the rule that lets a claim nobody believes delete a reader's assertion — is deleted rather than patched.
* Bad, because it is the most expensive of the three: a new field the model must state, a new validity rule, a new claim on the fixture, and a state's on-and-off representation in the solve.
* Bad, because it moves the prompt fingerprint, so it is locked to the one paid re-recording.

### (ii) Events only; a sustained push is two arrows

* Good, because it reproduces `sustain` exactly under first passage — an arrow from the event that starts the push and an inhibiting arrow from the event that ends it — at the cost of one validity rule and one sentence in the prompt.
* Good, because it adds no field, so it does not move the fingerprint and does not wait for the freeze. It is the cheapest sound option.
* Bad, because `mode` and the word *sustain* leave the vocabulary, and record 0005's best idea becomes a modelling convention rather than a thing the product knows about.
* Bad, because the reader has to know to draw two arrows for one mechanism, and nothing on screen says so.

### (iii) Keep today's snapshot meaning for states only

* Good, because nothing in the engine changes for those claims.
* Bad, because two claims side by side on one map would answer two different questions with one number in the same place, which is the thing two significant figures and a range exist to prevent.

## More Information

* **Kent's decision, 2026-09-21**, taken through the question tool: *"Events and states. Automatic retraction is deleted — 'Hormuz opens, then Iran is struck' leaves both events standing; the strike lowers the state the strait stays open through 1 November. Reverses record 0014, decision A. The model says which kind each claim is, so `persistence` rides the one shape freeze."* Recorded the same evening in the dated decisions note kept locally under `plans/notes/`.
* **The measurements.** The `sustain`-equals-`trigger` identity, the four-map spread that shows a state is not one yes/no fact, and the supposition voided by a claim at `.001` were all re-run on 2026-09-21 by this record's author, from scripts kept locally under `plans/analysis/scripts/`. The fingerprint pair and the count of `sustain` arrows in the committed recording are quoted from the adversarial pass of the same date, and the arrow count was re-counted independently: 19 accepted arrows, 6 `sustain`, 3 `impulse`, all six `sustain` arrows leaving claims of `kind: event`.
* **Related records.** Proposed ADR-0016 (which this record exists because of) · ADR-0005 (its `mode` table amended here) · ADR-0014 (its decision A reversed here) · ADR-0003 (the model proposes, our code disposes — which is why `persistence` is stated by the model and checked by us) · ADR-0006 (what we ask the model, amended at the freeze) · ADR-0012 (a recording is the real stream played back, which is why the six illegal arrows matter).
* **Chapters this rewrites.** `spec/multiverse/propagation.md` B4, `spec/multiverse/interventions.md`'s retraction passages, `spec/graph/link.md`, `spec/vocabulary.md`, and the tile chapter that owns the badge's geometry.

12	
13	# ADR-0021: What version one does not build
14	
15	> **The number is 0021 on purpose.** Records 0018, 0019 and 0020 are reserved for stack 06 — like with like, a stop is a price the reader owns, and quotes recorded first — by Kent's decisions of 2026-09-21, and are written when that stack opens.
16	
17	## Context and Problem Statement
18	
19	The definition of done says *"every decision — including every requirement cut — has an accepted record."* Six functional requirements and one invariant are being cut, and one requirement shrunk, and until this record exists all seven are cut nowhere and built nowhere. A reader comparing `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` against what ships would find them simply missing, which is the same shape of dishonesty as a number nobody computed.
20	
21	This record is short on purpose. One entry each: the requirement in its own words, and one sentence saying why it is not built.
22	
23	## Decision Drivers
24	
25	* **The definition of done.** Every cut requirement has a record, or the box does not tick.
26	* **The brief.** Nothing cut here is asked for by the assignment; each was our own addition to the roadmap.
27	* **The traceability veto** (Kent): a reader must be able to trace what is on screen — and what is absent — to a decision.
28	* **Where the remaining sessions go.** Stacks 05, 06 and 07 are the engine's soundness, the trade, and a map you can argue with. Everything below competes with those.
29	
30	## Considered Options
31	
32	* **A. Write one short record listing every cut, with a sentence each** — and amend the requirements themselves in the same pull request.
33	* **B. A record per cut.** Seven records saying one thing each.
34	* **C. Delete the requirements from `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` and say nothing.**
35	
36	## Decision Outcome
37	
38	Chosen option: **A**, because the cuts share one reason — they are research projects or dashboards competing with the three things the brief actually asks for — and seven records would make a reader read seven pages to learn one thing; and because option C is the traceability veto.
39	
40	### The cuts
41	
42	**FR-17 (P1)** — *"Compare ≥3 branches as small multiples; at most 4 branches visible, rest collapsed to a list; branches must be named."*
43	**Not built.** Three or more branches side by side is a dashboard, and the ranked change list already answers the question it would answer, two worlds at a time; how one ranking is read across three lists is undesigned and is an open question in the diff chapter rather than a plan item.
44	
45	**FR-18 (P1)** — *"`refine`: expand a proposition into sub-propositions; the children's combined likelihood must equal the parent's — they marginalize back (INV-10). This is the brainstorm's 'search deeper lines'."*
46	**Not built.** Making finer claims add back up to the claim they replace is marginalisation algebra on top of an exact core — a research project — and nothing in the brief asks for it.
47	
48	**INV-10** — *"Refinement adds up. After a proposition is split into finer sub-propositions, their combined likelihood equals the original's within a small tolerance."*
49	**Met by a named refusal, not by a feature.** The `refine` operation exists as a shape so nothing has to be retrofitted, and asking for it returns one violation with our own sentence: *"Splitting the claim … into finer claims is not built yet, so this edit cannot be folded onto this map"* (`backend/src/katalyst/domain/patch.py:657-691`, violation code `edit_not_applicable`, pinned by `test_splitting_a_claim_says_it_is_not_built_yet`). An invariant about an operation the product refuses to perform is satisfied by the refusal, and the definition of done says so in those words rather than leaving the box blank.
50	
51	**FR-20 (P2)** — *"Probes: attach a Monte Carlo, a Bayesian sub-net, or a persona red-team to one proposition; results re-enter as `simulated` beliefs with their own provenance and rationale."*
52	**Not built.** A Monte Carlo or a sub-net bolted onto one claim of an exact core is a second engine with a second set of answers to reconcile, and the honest part of the idea — a persona that argues with a step of the map — lands in stack 07 as *challenge this arrow*, on machinery that already exists.
53	
54	**FR-24 (P1), in part** — *"Payoff distribution from thousands of random simulations: the 10th / 50th / 90th-percentile outcomes, **the average loss in the worst 5% of runs (CVaR₅), the largest peak-to-trough loss, and the chance of being wiped out.** The actuarial 'wiped out' case gets its own row."*
55	**The three emphasised quantities are not built.** Each needs a capital base and a portfolio — how much the reader has, and what else they hold — and the product asks for neither, so all three would be arithmetic dressed as risk management. The percentile outcomes stay and are built in stack 06 from the reader's own position.
56	
57	**FR-29 (P2)** — *"Historical-analog panel: for a link, past instances and how prices moved around them, with an uncertainty band (an event study)."*
58	**Not built.** It needs dated past instances *and* the price history around them; record 0010's grounding has a live prediction-market read and a public economic-data read and nothing historical, and the base-rate work measured how thin the ground is — 93 searches across eighteen claims bought five reference classes, three of them counts of *0 of 2*, *2 of 3* and *1 of 1*.
59	
60	**FR-30 (P2)** — *"Pastcast self-test: run a chain on a resolved 2024–25 event with a date-frozen corpus and show the Brier score (the standard accuracy score for probability forecasts; lower is better), including when it is bad."*
61	**Not built.** It needs the evidence frozen as it stood before each event, which the generation pipeline cannot do — it searches the live web — and one resolved event is not a track record. One honest sentence about it goes on the *what I would do next* page.
62	
63	**A consequence of cutting FR-30, stated here so nobody has to find it.** FR-8 forbids an ensemble — *"no claim is asked about twice"* — and names exactly one condition that would reopen it: *"if FR-30's pastcast shows stated ranges missing badly against the evaluation scorecard."* Cutting FR-30 throws away the only key to that lock. **So no ensemble is built in version one, and nothing can reopen it within version one.** Record 0015 stands unchanged; this record only removes its escape hatch, and says so rather than letting a later plan schedule an ensemble anyway.
64	
65	### The one requirement shrunk rather than cut
66	
67	**FR-31 (P0)** — *"Sessions (graph + branches + transcripts) persist to a single SQLite file (a one-file database, no server) and are addressable by URL. No accounts in v1."*
68	
69	Today nothing is stored at all: the app keeps nothing between requests and no volume is declared (`ARCHITECTURE.md:173`). **Amended** (Kent, 2026-09-21) to what we already write:
70	
71	> **FR-31 (P0)** A finished generation is served back by its id from the same line-by-line file a recording is. One format, one loader, no database. Sessions are addressable by that id in the URL. No accounts in v1.
72	
73	A kept run is already written to disk as exactly that file, and the replay path already reads it. One format, one loader, one reader's habit — about one session, against two or three for a database the walk never exercises. Anti-pattern 12's closing clause, *"SQLite file on a volume"*, is amended with it: the file is the one we already write, and there is no database in version one at all.
74

status: proposed
date: 2026-09-21
decision-makers: Kent Gang

# ADR-0021: What version one does not build

> **The number is 0021 on purpose.** Records 0018, 0019 and 0020 are reserved for stack 06 — like with like, a stop is a price the reader owns, and quotes recorded first — by Kent's decisions of 2026-09-21, and are written when that stack opens.

## Context and Problem Statement

The definition of done says *"every decision — including every requirement cut — has an accepted record."* Six functional requirements and one invariant are being cut, and one requirement shrunk, and until this record exists all seven are cut nowhere and built nowhere. A reader comparing `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` against what ships would find them simply missing, which is the same shape of dishonesty as a number nobody computed.

This record is short on purpose. One entry each: the requirement in its own words, and one sentence saying why it is not built.

## Decision Drivers

* **The definition of done.** Every cut requirement has a record, or the box does not tick.
* **The brief.** Nothing cut here is asked for by the assignment; each was our own addition to the roadmap.
* **The traceability veto** (Kent): a reader must be able to trace what is on screen — and what is absent — to a decision.
* **Where the remaining sessions go.** Stacks 05, 06 and 07 are the engine's soundness, the trade, and a map you can argue with. Everything below competes with those.

## Considered Options

* **A. Write one short record listing every cut, with a sentence each** — and amend the requirements themselves in the same pull request.
* **B. A record per cut.** Seven records saying one thing each.
* **C. Delete the requirements from `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` and say nothing.**

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **A**, because the cuts share one reason — they are research projects or dashboards competing with the three things the brief actually asks for — and seven records would make a reader read seven pages to learn one thing; and because option C is the traceability veto.

### The cuts

**FR-17 (P1)** — *"Compare ≥3 branches as small multiples; at most 4 branches visible, rest collapsed to a list; branches must be named."*
**Not built.** Three or more branches side by side is a dashboard, and the ranked change list already answers the question it would answer, two worlds at a time; how one ranking is read across three lists is undesigned and is an open question in the diff chapter rather than a plan item.

**FR-18 (P1)** — *"`refine`: expand a proposition into sub-propositions; the children's combined likelihood must equal the parent's — they marginalize back (INV-10). This is the brainstorm's 'search deeper lines'."*
**Not built.** Making finer claims add back up to the claim they replace is marginalisation algebra on top of an exact core — a research project — and nothing in the brief asks for it.

**INV-10** — *"Refinement adds up. After a proposition is split into finer sub-propositions, their combined likelihood equals the original's within a small tolerance."*
**Met by a named refusal, not by a feature.** The `refine` operation exists as a shape so nothing has to be retrofitted, and asking for it returns one violation with our own sentence: *"Splitting the claim … into finer claims is not built yet, so this edit cannot be folded onto this map"* (`backend/src/katalyst/domain/patch.py:657-691`, violation code `edit_not_applicable`, pinned by `test_splitting_a_claim_says_it_is_not_built_yet`). An invariant about an operation the product refuses to perform is satisfied by the refusal, and the definition of done says so in those words rather than leaving the box blank.

**FR-20 (P2)** — *"Probes: attach a Monte Carlo, a Bayesian sub-net, or a persona red-team to one proposition; results re-enter as `simulated` beliefs with their own provenance and rationale."*
**Not built.** A Monte Carlo or a sub-net bolted onto one claim of an exact core is a second engine with a second set of answers to reconcile, and the honest part of the idea — a persona that argues with a step of the map — lands in stack 07 as *challenge this arrow*, on machinery that already exists.

**FR-24 (P1), in part** — *"Payoff distribution from thousands of random simulations: the 10th / 50th / 90th-percentile outcomes, **the average loss in the worst 5% of runs (CVaR₅), the largest peak-to-trough loss, and the chance of being wiped out.** The actuarial 'wiped out' case gets its own row."*
**The three emphasised quantities are not built.** Each needs a capital base and a portfolio — how much the reader has, and what else they hold — and the product asks for neither, so all three would be arithmetic dressed as risk management. The percentile outcomes stay and are built in stack 06 from the reader's own position.

**FR-29 (P2)** — *"Historical-analog panel: for a link, past instances and how prices moved around them, with an uncertainty band (an event study)."*
**Not built.** It needs dated past instances *and* the price history around them; record 0010's grounding has a live prediction-market read and a public economic-data read and nothing historical, and the base-rate work measured how thin the ground is — 93 searches across eighteen claims bought five reference classes, three of them counts of *0 of 2*, *2 of 3* and *1 of 1*.

**FR-30 (P2)** — *"Pastcast self-test: run a chain on a resolved 2024–25 event with a date-frozen corpus and show the Brier score (the standard accuracy score for probability forecasts; lower is better), including when it is bad."*
**Not built.** It needs the evidence frozen as it stood before each event, which the generation pipeline cannot do — it searches the live web — and one resolved event is not a track record. One honest sentence about it goes on the *what I would do next* page.

**A consequence of cutting FR-30, stated here so nobody has to find it.** FR-8 forbids an ensemble — *"no claim is asked about twice"* — and names exactly one condition that would reopen it: *"if FR-30's pastcast shows stated ranges missing badly against the evaluation scorecard."* Cutting FR-30 throws away the only key to that lock. **So no ensemble is built in version one, and nothing can reopen it within version one.** Record 0015 stands unchanged; this record only removes its escape hatch, and says so rather than letting a later plan schedule an ensemble anyway.

### The one requirement shrunk rather than cut

**FR-31 (P0)** — *"Sessions (graph + branches + transcripts) persist to a single SQLite file (a one-file database, no server) and are addressable by URL. No accounts in v1."*

Today nothing is stored at all: the app keeps nothing between requests and no volume is declared (`ARCHITECTURE.md:173`). **Amended** (Kent, 2026-09-21) to what we already write:

> **FR-31 (P0)** A finished generation is served back by its id from the same line-by-line file a recording is. One format, one loader, no database. Sessions are addressable by that id in the URL. No accounts in v1.

A kept run is already written to disk as exactly that file, and the replay path already reads it. One format, one loader, one reader's habit — about one session, against two or three for a database the walk never exercises. Anti-pattern 12's closing clause, *"SQLite file on a volume"*, is amended with it: the file is the one we already write, and there is no database in version one at all.

### Cut in the same pass, touching no requirement

Listed so the roadmap and this record agree, one line each.

* **Undoing an edit (*Release*)** — in no requirement, no invariant and no clause of the brief; it is a change to the domain, the wire and the generated types wearing a button.
* **A probability slider** — every edit appends to an audit trail with no undo, so scrubbing writes thirty edits or opens a second, unaudited path. *Change this push* is the honest version and exists.
* **Drafting a whole map in one streamed call** — it was a speed idea, and the demonstration runs from a recording; the quality case for it went when the generated map turned out not to be a tree.
* **Unrolling feedback arrows over time** — INV-6's checkable half stands and is tested (no cycles once feedback arrows are set aside; every feedback arrow carries a delay above zero); unrolling them in the engine is asked for nowhere.
* **A fifth, price-valued kind of claim, and two-sided payoffs** — a position already carries the spot price, the volatility and the horizon, none of which a model can supply; and the losing leg *is* the stop. Record 0013's two payoff shapes are unchanged.
* **Screenshot baselines and a wall-clock gate in the build** — two reliable sources of failures that mean nothing.

### Cut nowhere, and belonging to another record

So that this record cannot be read as the complete list of everything absent:

* **The path product** (FR-11 and INV-8) is replaced, not cut, by proposed record 0016.
* **The derived stop-loss** (INV-14, FR-22, FR-23 and the rest of FR-24) is reshaped by proposed record 0019 in stack 06.
* **Kalshi**, the third venue named in FR-26, belongs to proposed record 0020 in stack 06.
* **The other three example inputs** (FR-3) are not cut: all four are recorded once, together, at stack 05's shape freeze.

### Consequences

* Good, because a reader can hold `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` beside the product and account for every line.
* Good, because the definition of done's *"every decision has an accepted record"* becomes true rather than aspirational.
* Good, because roughly five to six sessions of work move off the plan and onto the *what I would do next* page, where they can be described honestly instead of half-built.
* Bad, because two P0 and two P1 requirements are affected, and a reviewer who read the roadmap first will find less than it promised. The requirements themselves carry the amendment, so the promise and its retraction sit in one place.
* Bad, because cutting FR-30 leaves the product with no measurement of whether its numbers are any good — the honest sentence on the *what I would do next* page is the whole of the answer.
* Neutral, because nothing here is hard to revisit: each cut is a feature nobody has started.

### Confirmation

* Every requirement named above carries, in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md`, a dated line pointing at this record — so the cut is found by a reader of the requirements, not only by a reader of the records.
* `test_splitting_a_claim_says_it_is_not_built_yet` — INV-10's named refusal, already green.
* `grep -rn "ensemble" backend/src` finds nothing (record 0015's check, which this record keeps in force permanently).
* The definition of done's line *"every invariant has a named test — INV-10 by a named refusal, and this list says so"* names the test above.
* A review item at stack 07: the *what I would do next* page names the pastcast, the probes, `refine`, the analog panel and small multiples, each in one sentence, and does not claim any of them is nearly done.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. One short record listing every cut (chosen)

* Good, because the cuts share one reason and a reader learns it once.
* Good, because it is one place to look when a later plan tries to schedule one of them again.
* Bad, because a single record covering seven decisions is harder to supersede one line at a time; a later record naming the requirement it revives is the answer.

### B. A record per cut

* Good, because each could be superseded on its own.
* Bad, because seven pages that each say *not built, because nothing asks for it* teach a reader nothing and hide the one reason they share.

### C. Delete the requirements and say nothing

* Good, because it is the least writing.
* Bad, because it is the traceability veto in its plainest form: a requirement that vanishes cannot be traced to a decision, and a reviewer comparing the roadmap with the product would rightly not trust either.

## More Information

* **Kent's decisions, 2026-09-21**, taken through the question tool: *"Shrink FR-31 to the file we already write — a finished generation served back by its id from the same line-by-line file a recording is. One format, one loader, no database."* And the list of cuts he named in the same sitting. Recorded that evening in the dated decisions note kept locally under `plans/notes/`.
* **The count that prompted this record**: the adversarial pass of 2026-09-21, finding S6 — six functional requirements cut with no record at all, against a definition of done requiring one for every decision.
* **Related records.** ADR-0015 (no ensemble; this record removes the one condition that would have reopened it) · ADR-0013 (the two payoff shapes, unchanged by the refusal of a fifth kind of claim) · ADR-0010 (the grounding sources, which is why the historical-analog panel has nothing to read) · ADR-0012 (recordings, which is the file FR-31 now uses) · proposed ADR-0016 and ADR-0017 (the engine; they replace rather than cut) · records 0018, 0019 and 0020, reserved for stack 06.

+
+**Proposed, not in force.** This amendment takes effect **when proposed records 0016 and 0017 are accepted**, and not before. Amended in place rather than superseded, because the shape of the decision does not change: one number and one sentence per arrow, the arrows add on a scale where independent pushes add instead of multiplying, and every rejected option stays rejected.
+
+### What proposed record 0016 changes here
+
+It keeps the arrow's fields and changes what they bend. `strength`, `lag`, `shape`, `half_life` and `reflexive` keep their names and their meanings; they now bend a **rate** — how likely a claim is to happen on each day — rather than a likelihood read on one day, and the claim's number is that rate added up across its window. Five passages move:
+
+1. **The aggregation formula** — the code block beginning `log-odds P(child, t) = log-odds(prior_child) + …` and the sentence under it beginning *"In words: start from the child's own base likelihood…"*. The arrows still add; what they add to is the rate, not the day's likelihood.
+2. **The execution paragraph** — *"Execution is Monte Carlo — thousands of random simulations whose spread is the answer. Draw `N` seeded worlds (default 10 000). In each, every proposition is sampled parents-first from its aggregated log-odds."* Replaced by two passes: one forward pass for *when* each cause arrives, then an exact solve over yes/no truths for *whether* each claim happens. Worlds still exist and are still drawn, parents first; they are drawn **from** the answer rather than **being** the answer.
+3. **Learning by keeping only the consistent draws** — *"learning fixes a value and keeps only the draws consistent with it (warn loudly when fewer than about 2% survive)"*, and the paragraph beginning *"Keeping only the consistent draws is why learning reaches further than asserting…"*. The **rule** stands exactly: observing a claim may move its causes and supposing it may not (INV-3), and the affected sets of the 2026-09-17 amendment are untouched. The **mechanism** changes: nothing is thrown away, so nothing can starve.
+4. **What a belief is** — *"A belief is the share of worlds in which the proposition came out true"*. It is the chance the claim happens by its deadline, worked out exactly rather than counted.
+5. **The interval**, already amended on 2026-09-17 to point at record 0014, is amended again there and not here.
+
+**Untouched:** the link-fields table apart from its `mode` row; *"elicitation is one number and one sentence per link"*; two significant figures and the interval on the canvas; the withdrawn staged-delivery paragraph, which stays visible as history; and every option this record rejected — per-combination tables, scenario trees, Markov steady states, role-played simulation and model narration. Where the two numbers on an arrow come from is changed by the shape freeze at the end of stack 05, which amends record 0006, not this record.
+
+### What proposed record 0017 changes here
+
+**The `mode` row of the link-fields table**, which today reads *"`sustain` — the effect holds only while the parent holds; remove the parent and it retracts"*. Under record 0016 nothing that has happened can un-happen, so measured on the same map a `sustain` arrow and a `trigger` arrow produce the identical number — `0.442471` against `0.442471` — and `mode` becomes dead data. Record 0017 gives it a job back: a `sustain` arrow may leave **only** a claim that can stop holding — a *state*. The row is rewritten to say so.
+
+With it: the consequence bullet beginning *"Good, because `trigger` versus `sustain` makes the Hormuz-then-strike branch behave correctly"* — the pair still works, and what it works on is a state rather than a retraction; and the two confirmation tests `test_trigger_persists_after_parent_reset` and `test_sustain_retracts_when_parent_removed`, which are replaced by record 0017's own named tests.
+
+**This record's judgement stands.** Trigger versus sustain was called *"the best idea in the brainstorm"* and it survives — as a distinction about what kind of claim an arrow may leave, rather than one about what happens when a parent is taken away.

A claim the user supposed true stays supposed until another edit changes it; nothing withdraws it on a schedule *(rewritten 2026-09-21; decision record 0017)*.

## 8. Two ordering rules that are not edits

1. **The generated numbers file must exist before the flip.** One committed file owning every number the worked example quotes, regenerated by the build, failing on a difference. 1	# Red team — `design-after-midpoint-review.md` and `PLAN.md`
2	
3	**2026-09-21 · one read-only Opus analyst · no file in the repository or any worktree was
4	changed.** Scripts at
5	`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kentgang-git3-katalyst/b70a1857-a894-4bbe-b3a6-4d7cf3ebc4f8/scratchpad/digest/redteam/`
6	(`rt_core.py`, `attack1.py`…`attack4.py`). I ran no paid call, no server, no whole suite, no
7	playwright. **PROVED** means I ran it or read it; **SUSPECT** means I argued it and did not
8	measure it. Every number below is mine unless I say otherwise.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Verdict
13	
14	**Sound with changes — but three of them are load-bearing and one is a straight error of
15	fact.** The engine reformulation is the right idea, the hazard model is right, the collapse
16	from event *times* to event *truths* is a genuinely good trade, and `Suppose this is true` comes
17	out exact to four decimal places; I could not break that. What is not true is the word
18	**exact**: under `This happened` the design does exact arithmetic on a table built from the
19	wrong timing, and I measured **0.124** of error on a four-claim map — twenty-five times the
20	worst gap the design quotes, on the product's second verb. Separately, `sustain` does not
21	survive §2.2 — so the event/state split is **required**, not optional, and the decision put to
22	Kent as a free choice is not one; and the cost line ("3 sessions, net −350 lines") is scoped to
23	the one file where the work is cheapest and omits `diff.py`, the browser, 60 tests and ~400
24	lines of spec.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## 2. Must change before Kent sees it
29	
30	### M1. "Solved exactly" is false under *This happened*. The design must say so and state a tolerance. — **PROVED**
31	
32	The design (§2.2): *"Whether each claim happens is then solved exactly … `This happened`
33	multiplies in the evidence and renormalises. Both exact."* The arithmetic is exact. **The table
34	it is applied to is not**, and an observation is exactly the operation that invalidates it.
35	
36	The forward pass produces each claim's arrival-time distribution **under the prior**. Evidence
37	moves a claim's arrival as well as its truth ("if B happened, A more likely happened early"),
38	and the design never rebuilds the tables. `do` is fine, because the design explicitly re-runs
39	the forward pass under it. `observe` is not.
40	
41	I wrote a faithful implementation of §2.2 (`rt_core.py`) and an exact-over-times reference,
42	with **all three arrow shapes** — the analyst's scripts use `step` only; the string `shape`
43	never appears in `ve_cost.py`, `pin_error.py` or `pin_error_many.py`, so the quoted .0065 and
44	.049 have never met an `impulse`, the one shape where timing is everything.
45	
46	Worst |design − exact| by map family (`attack1.py`, K = 24):
47	
48	| map | worst gap | where |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| the analyst's own map, my code (control) | .0022 | — |
51	| impulse, short half-life, near a deadline | .0001 | *(the design is fine here — see below)* |
52	| diamond, equal lags | .0055 | observe |
53	| chain, depth 6 / depth 10 | .0090 / .0109 | observe |
54	| diamond, lags 2 vs 34 | .0125 | observe |
55	| **strong inhibitor** | **.0229** | observe |
56	| **lag 26 days against a 28-day gap** | **.0338** | observe |
57	| **"race against the clock" chain, lag 9 of a 12-day gap** | **.0352** | observe |
58	
59	**Every gap over .01 is an observation.** Over 140 adversarially generated four-claim maps
60	(`attack2.py` §B, tight deadlines, lags up to 70 % of each gap, mixed shapes — 9 520 compared
61	numbers):
62	
63	| query | n | mean | p99 | worst | **share off by more than .005** |
64	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
65	| no edit | 560 | .00027 | .0046 | .0175 | 0.9 % |
66	| `do` (Suppose) | 4 480 | .00007 | .0015 | .0259 | **0.2 %** |
67	| `observe` (This happened) | 4 480 | .00127 | .0151 | **.2043** | **6.6 %** |
68	
69	The worst case re-run at a finer grid is **not** a grid artefact: at K = 40 it is **.1242**
70	(exact .6318, design .5076), stable. Its shape: three parents, impulse arrows with long lags,
71	and an observation on a claim that is *also* a parent of another parent — so the evidence
72	shifts the second parent's arrival and the table never learns. In-degree 3 is what generation

391	- **The analyst's own measurements are honest.** `pin_error.py` reproduces PIN .1534 / AVG
392	  **.0065**; `pin_error_many.py` reproduces mean .00105, p99 .01872, worst **.04920**, 97.2 %
393	  within .01. I did not re-run `ve_cost.py`/`ve_cost2.py` (timing only, and heavy on a shared
394	  machine).
395	- **The collapse from times to truths is the right trade, and `Suppose` is exact.** Across 4 480
396	  `do` queries on adversarial maps the mean gap is .00007 and 99.8 % are inside .005. §2.2's
397	  central idea survives everything I threw at it *except* conditioning.
398	- **The impulse is not the problem I expected it to be.** Impulse arrows with half-lives of 1–2
399	  days landing 4 days before a deadline gave gaps of **.0000–.0001**. Because the design
400	  integrates the whole area of the impulse, ADR-0014's wart really does go. Impulses only hurt
401	  in combination with an observation (M1).
402	- **`Verdict.product → None` is genuinely backend-only.** `apiSource.ts:272` and

409	- **Several generation counts are exactly right**: 2 of 20 `LinkProposal`s; 93 searches / five

420	
421	## 5. What I could not check
